nodes.title: Geometric and arithmetic Hilbert weight spaces, bounded smooth weights, and the map rho from W to W* (with the sign discrepancy in BHW Definition 6.1)
nodes.statement: Let T := Res_{O_F|Z} G_m, so T(Z_p) = O_p^x where O_p = O_F (x) Z_p (p is not assumed unramified in F), and let L be the fixed perfectoid field extension of Q_p^cyc. The weight space for G = Res_{F/Q} GL_2 is W := Spf(Z_p[[T(Z_p) x Z_p^x]])^an_eta x L and the weight space for G* is W* := Spf(Z_p[[T(Z_p)]])^an_eta x L. An L-point of W is a pair (w,t) of continuous characters w: T(Z_p) -> L^x and t: Z_p^x -> L^x; an L-point of W* is a character T(Z_p) -> L^x. A weight is a morphism kappa: U -> W (for G) or kappa: U -> W* (for G*), where U is a smooth rigid space over some perfectoid field extension of L; kappa is bounded if its image lies in some affinoid open subspace. A weight kappa: U -> W* is the same as a morphism kappa: O_p^x x U -> hat-G_m, and it is bounded iff |T_kappa| := sup_{(t,x) in O_p^x x U} |kappa(t,x) - 1| < 1. A weight kappa: U -> W gives maps w_kappa: O_p^x x U -> hat-G_m and t_kappa: Z_p^x x U -> hat-G_m, and is regarded as the G*-weight rho(w_kappa, t_kappa). BHW Definition 6.1 defines rho as the morphism attached to the group map T(Z_p) -> T(Z_p) x Z_p^x, x |-> (x^2, N_{F/Q}(x)), and in the same sentence writes kappa = w^2 * (t^{-1} o N_{F/Q}) for the image of (w,t) (again rho(w_kappa,t_kappa) = w_kappa^2 * (t_kappa^{-1} o N_{F/Q}) on p. 1757). These two descriptions disagree by an inversion of t: pulling characters back along x |-> (x^2, N(x)) gives w^2 * (t o N), whereas the displayed formula is the pull-back along x |-> (x^2, N_{F/Q}(x)^{-1}). This roadmap pins the displayed character formula kappa = w^2 * (t^{-1} o N_{F/Q}) together with the group map x |-> (x^2, N_{F/Q}(x)^{-1}); the discrepancy is recorded, not silently resolved.

nodes.statement: Neighbourhoods: embed G_a -> P^1 by z |-> (z : 1) and apply Res_{O_F|Z}; for r in (0,1] cap |L|, B_r(O_p : 1) subset Res_{O_F|Z} hat-G_a is the union of the balls of radius r around the points (a : 1), a in O_p, and B_r(O_p^x : 1) is defined analogously; B_0(O_p : 1) := O_p as a profinite perfectoid space (Definitions 5.16-5.17). In the elliptic case (Definitions 2.2, 3.10) B_r(Z_p^x : 1) is, for r < 1, an adic group thickening of Z_p^x. nodes.title: Left action on infinite-level level structures, pull-back of functions and sections, and the resulting automorphy-factor law
nodes.statement: Conventions fixed once, following BHW. (i) Level action: gamma in GL_2(Z_p) (elliptic, (2.1)), in G*(Z_p) (Definition 5.14) or in G(Z/p^n) acting on the hybrid spaces (Definition 8.8) acts on moduli data by gamma . (A, iota, lambda, mu, alpha) = (A, iota, lambda, mu, alpha o gamma^vee), where alpha: O_p^2 -> T_p A^vee (resp. Z_p^2 -> T_p E) and gamma^vee := det(gamma) gamma^{-1}; composing with gamma^vee rather than gamma^{-1} is what makes this a LEFT action (Remark 5.8). (ii) Functions pull back by gamma^* f := f o gamma, so (gamma_1 gamma_2)^* = gamma_2^* gamma_1^*. (iii) The Hodge-Tate period map is equivariant, and on the pulled-back coordinate z (on the anticanonical locus) gamma^* z = (a z + b)/(c z + d) for gamma = (a b; c d) in Gamma_0(p) (equation (3.1), from the Moebius action of Lemma 2.4, which preserves B_r(Z_p : 1)). (iv) On P^1 the Gamma_0(p)-equivariant structure of O(1) compatible with (2.1) lets gamma act through det(gamma)^{-1} gamma, so gamma^{-1} acts as gamma^vee, and a section s pulls back as gamma^* s := gamma^{-1} o s o gamma (proof of Lemma 3.19). Consequently an automorphy factor j(gamma, x) used in a transformation law gamma^* f = j(gamma)^{-1} f is compatible with composition exactly when j(gamma_1 gamma_2, x) = j(gamma_1, gamma_2 x) j(gamma_2, x) (left-action cocycle law); for j = gamma^* s / s with s a nowhere-vanishing section this law is automatic.

nodes.title: The automorphy-twisted invariant subsheaf of the push-forward along a pro-etale torsor of a weight family, and its module structure
nodes.statement: Setting of BHW Lemma 3.7 and Definitions 3.15, 6.5, 9.1: Y an affinoid adic space over L which is a smooth rigid space or a perfectoid space; Gamma a profinite group; X in Y_proet an affinoid perfectoid pro-etale Gamma-torsor; U a smooth adic space over L; X_U := X x_L U and Y_U := Y x_L U (sousperfectoid, BHW Corollaries 3.4-3.5) with induced map h: X_U -> Y_U. Lemma 3.7: (h_* O^+_{X_U})^Gamma = O^+_{Y_U} and (h_* O_{X_U})^Gamma = O_{Y_U}. Construction (the pattern of Definitions 3.15, 6.5 and 9.1, where all infinite-level sheaves are pushed forward to the finite-level base): given invertible functions j(gamma) in O^+(X_U)^x for gamma in Gamma, set omega_j(V) := {f in h_* O_{X_U}(V) : gamma^* f = j(gamma)^{-1} f for all gamma in Gamma} and omega_j^+(V) := {f in h_* O^+_{X_U}(V) : gamma^* f = j(gamma)^{-1} f for all gamma}. These are subsheaves of h_* O and h_* O^+ (intersections of equalizers of the sheaf maps f |-> gamma^* f and f |-> j(gamma)^{-1} f), stable under multiplication by (h_* O)^Gamma = O_{Y_U} (resp. O^+_{Y_U}), hence sheaves of O_{Y_U}- (resp. O^+_{Y_U}-) modules; for j = 1 they equal O_{Y_U} and O^+_{Y_U}. An equivariant morphism of torsors (along a group homomorphism) under which the factors pull back to each other induces a morphism of the corresponding twisted sheaves; BHW use this in (9.2), Lemma 10.1 and Lemma 10.3. No local freeness is claimed at this level of generality.
hypotheses: Exactly the hypotheses of Lemma 3.7: Y affinoid over L and either smooth rigid or perfectoid; Gamma profinite; X affinoid perfectoid and a pro-etale Gamma-torsor in Y_proet; U smooth over L
The torsor hypothesis is only available away from the cusps in the elliptic case; the boundary needs Proposition 3.8 (see O2)

Smooth rigid Y: in Y_proet, O^+_X(X) = hat-O^+_{Y_proet}(X) because X is affinoid perfectoid; the Cartesian torsor diagram gives O^+_X(X)^Gamma = hat-O^+_{Y_proet}(X)^Gamma = hat-O^+_{Y_proet}(Y); Lemma 3.6 identifies this with O^+_Y(Y); invert p for O.
